run.question: My signup service is failing and users can't register. What should I check to debug this issue?

report.summary: Fetched runbook signup-service-debugging-runbook and carried out its steps with my own tools, as far as the available tools allow. Step 1 (signup status): namespace app-162 holds two signup-service pods and one payments-service pod, all Phase Running with restartCount 0, but all three are Ready=False/ContainersReady=False and their containers have been running since 17:02:07 without any restart. Step 2 (payments health): the payments-service pod is the failing dependency — its own log says 'STRIPE_API_KEY is set to invalid test key - service will fail' and 'Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key', and it answers /ready and /health with 503. Step 3 (service-to-service): kubectl exec probing was not possible (no exec tool), but the signup pod logs show 'Payments service check failed: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>' toward http://payments-service:8080, and the Endpoints for payments-service and signup-service list only notReadyAddresses, so neither ClusterIP currently has a ready backend. Step 4 (payments-specific checks): the Stripe log lines were found; no database-specific lines appeared in the sampled log, and DATABASE_URL comes from a Secret key I cannot read. Step 5 (env vars): the deployment spec maps STRIPE_API_KEY and DATABASE_URL from Secret app-162/payments-secrets (keys stripe-api-key, database-url); the Secret's values are unreadable, so the 'invalid test key' statement rests on the application's own log, not on reading the secret. Kubernetes wiring looks correct (Services select app=payments-service / app=signup-service on port 8080, no NetworkPolicy objects exist, no ResourceQuota objects exist, no Ingress exists), which rules out policy/quota/ingress misconfiguration as far as these objects show. The otel-demo flagd fault-injection file still lists paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable, but both are defaultVariant 'off' and they target otel-demo's payment service, a different entity from app-162/payments-service. Prometheus and Jaeger were both unreachable (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so there are no metrics or traces for this incident and no evidence about user registration requests themselves; the user-facing impact is unverified. Conclusion is partial: the failing component and the credential fault are evidenced, but the Secret's actual value and any history of when it became invalid could not be observed.

claims.text: Namespace app-162 runs exactly three application pods: payments-service-6d94c44fdc-ctvsf, signup-service-7c89545dc9-6ncfd and signup-service-7c89545dc9-jvrlj; all are Phase Running, app labels payments-service/signup-service, and each has restartCount 0.

All three app-162 pods report condition Ready=False and ContainersReady=False; their single containers are in state running (startedAt 2026-11-23T17:02:07Z) with empty lastState, and pods were created at 2026-11-23T17:02:06Z/17:02:07Z under ReplicaSets payments-service-6d94c44fdc and signup-service-7c89545dc9.

payments-service-6d94c44fdc-ctvsf logged at 2026-11-23T17:02:08.999Z 'ERROR - STRIPE_API_KEY is set to invalid test key - service will fail', then at 17:02:17.377Z 'ERROR - Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key', and its own probe endpoints answered 503: 'GET /ready HTTP/1.1" 503' at 17:02:13, 17:02:18, 17:02:23 and 'GET /health HTTP/1.1" 503' at 17:02:17.

Both signup pods log repeated 'ERROR - Payments service check failed: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>' followed by their own 'GET /ready HTTP/1.1" 503' every 5 seconds at 17:02:13, 17:02:18 and 17:02:23 (pod signup-service-7c89545dc9-6ncfd), and the sibling pod signup-service-7c89545dc9-jvrlj logged the identical sequence and its own 503 /ready responses at the same times.

Deployment payments-service in app-162 defines env STRIPE_API_KEY from secretKeyRef name=payments-secrets key=stripe-api-key and DATABASE_URL from secretKeyRef name=payments-secrets key=database-url (PORT=8080); Deployment signup-service defines PAYMENTS_SERVICE_URL=http://payments-service:8080, DATABASE_URL from secretKeyRef name=signup-secrets key=database-url (PORT=8080), with readiness probes on /ready (periodSeconds 5) and liveness probes on /health.

Endpoints for app-162 services show no ready addresses: payments-service has only notReadyAddresses 10.244.0.52 (targetRef Pod payments-service-6d94c44fdc-ctvsf) and signup-service has only notReadyAddresses 10.244.0.50 and 10.244.0.51 (targetRefs the two signup-service pods), both on port 8080.

The Kubernetes Services signup-service (ClusterIP 10.96.194.213, selector app=signup-service, port 8080→8080) and payments-service (ClusterIP 10.96.189.124, selector app=payments-service, port 8080→8080) exist and their selectors match the running pods' app labels, so name resolution/selector wiring to the pods is consistent.

Events in app-162 at 17:02:06–17:02:07Z are only rollout normal events: Deployment signup-service 'Scaled up replica set signup-service-7c89545dc9 from 0 to 2', Deployment payments-service 'Scaled up replica set payments-service-6d94c44fdc from 0 to 1', ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate for the three pods, and Pod Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started for those pods; a grouped count of in-window events also recorded one Pod event with reason Unhealthy in app-162.

A cluster-wide query for NetworkPolicy objects returned zero items and a cluster-wide query for ResourceQuota objects returned zero items, so no NetworkPolicy or ResourceQuota object exists that could be blocking or throttling the signup→payments calls; a cluster-wide query for Ingress objects also returned zero items, so no HTTP entry point for registration was observed in these objects.

The only ConfigMap in app-162 is kube-root-ca.crt (key ca.crt); app-162 contains no fault-injection or application configuration ConfigMap, while ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config holds demo.flagd.json whose paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable flags both have defaultVariant 'off'.

The credential consumed as STRIPE_API_KEY from Secret app-162/payments-secrets (key stripe-api-key) is an invalid/test value, which makes payments-service fail its own /health and /ready checks with 503; because the pod never becomes Ready, the payments-service ClusterIP has no endpoint, so signup-service's call to http://payments-service:8080 is refused and every signup pod's /ready returns 503 — i.e. registration fails through the payments dependency rather than through signup's own code or database.

The signup and payments pods show no crash, eviction or OOM evidence: all three are Phase Running with restartCount 0, containers running with empty lastState, no previous container instance exists for any of them, and the in-window events contain no Evicted, OOMKilled, BackOff or Failed reason — the failure is a readiness/health-check failure, not a crashloop.

Fault-injection via the otel-demo flagd configuration (flags paymentFailure / paymentUnreachable, which describe payment failures and unreachability) was considered and rejected as the cause here: both flags' defaultVariant is 'off', and flagd-config lives in namespace otel-demo and drives the otel-demo services, not the separate app-162 signup-service/payments-service workloads.

A Kubernetes Service/selector, NetworkPolicy or ResourceQuota misconfiguration was considered as the reason signup cannot reach payments and rejected for the checked objects: the payments-service selector app=payments-service matches the running payments pod, zero NetworkPolicy objects exist cluster-wide and zero ResourceQuota objects exist, and the endpoints controller did resolve the pod into the payments-service endpoint set (as notReadyAddresses) rather than leaving it unselected.

Follow the runbook's resolution path: verify and correct the value of key stripe-api-key in Secret app-162/payments-secrets (only cluster administrators can read it), then roll deployment/payments-service so the pod picks up the corrected key, and confirm 'GET /health' and 'GET /ready' return 200 and that the payments-service Endpoints lose their notReadyAddresses entry; signup pods should then pass their /ready check on the next 5-second period.

Also verify the other Secret-backed settings that could not be read before declaring the signup path healthy: payments-secrets/database-url and signup-secrets/database-url — after payments recovers, re-read signup logs for database errors and, if a probing tool were available, test connectivity from a signup pod to http://payments-service:8080/health (runbook Step 3, not executable with the tools of this Run) and enable Prometheus/Jaeger scraping for the app-162 namespace so error rate and latency can be checked instead of only logs.

gaps: Secrets cannot be read: the actual STRIPE_API_KEY value in Secret app-162/payments-secrets (key stripe-api-key) and the database-url values in payments-secrets and signup-secrets are unverified; the 'invalid test key' conclusion rests on the payments-service application log, not on reading the secret.

Prometheus was unreachable for this Run (traces/list-services, get_metric_names and execute_prometheus_instant_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no error-rate, request-count or latency series for signup-service or payments-service could be read and none is reported; that absence is unqueried data, not a zero reading.

Jaeger was unreachable as well (traces_list_services and traces_search returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so there are no spans, no parent-child call edges and no per-request failure counts; the signup→payments dependency direction comes from the signup log text and the PAYMENTS_SERVICE_URL setting, not from traces.

No traces/metrics and no Ingress object were available to observe actual registration requests, so user-facing impact ('users can't register') is unverified beyond signup's own 503 /ready responses and payments' 503 /health and /ready.

All app-162 objects are only about 20–60 seconds old at query time (pods created 2026-11-23T17:02:06–07Z) and events outside the authorized window were dropped, so when the invalid key was introduced, whether the workload existed and was failing earlier in the 30-day window, and what changed are unknown; the change_history integration is not configured.
Database connectivity for payments-service and signup-service is unknown: no database/postgres log lines appeared in the sampled containers' logs and DATABASE_URL is a Secret reference.
kubectl exec/curl service-to-service testing (runbook Steps 3 and 5) could not be carried out because no exec tool is available in this Run.
next_steps: Read Secret app-162/payments-secrets key stripe-api-key as a cluster administrator and replace the invalid test value with a valid key; confirm both keys (stripe-api-key, database-url) exist on that Secret.
After correcting the key, roll deployment/payments-service and check the pod's log for absence of 'Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key' and 200 responses on /health and /ready.
Watch the payments-service Endpoints object for a ready address, then re-read both signup pods' logs and confirm /ready returns 200 (readiness periodSeconds is 5).
Run the runbook's connectivity test manually from a signup pod (curl -v http://payments-service:8080/health) and validate DATABASE_URL for both services once the key issue is resolved.
Enable Prometheus scraping/remote-write and Jaeger tracing for the app-162 namespace so future signup failures can be confirmed with error-rate and latency data rather than logs alone.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
